name: Isoniazid + Rifampicin
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Rifampicin is mainly cleared by the liver, and isoniazid by acetylation (50% to 70% of a dose appears in urine). The Irish label gives no kidney dose adjustment for the fixed combination but warns that isoniazid can cause a cerebellar syndrome, mainly in chronic kidney disease, and peripheral neuropathy. Hemodialysis removes isoniazid (advised for refractory overdose). It has no US FDA label for the combination.
kidney_function_basis: The SmPC does not grade kidney impairment; bands shown on creatinine clearance (CrCl).

bands.recommendation: Usual: rifampicin about 10 mg/kg (450 to 600 mg) with isoniazid about 5 mg/kg once daily, 30 minutes before or 2 hours after a meal (SmPC).
No kidney dose adjustment stated (SmPC). Pyridoxine for patients at risk of neuropathy.

No dose change for isoniazid or rifampicin at CrCl <30 (ATS/CDC/IDSA 2016; MSF); the SmPC asks for careful monitoring in severe renal dysfunction. Isoniazid can cause a cerebellar syndrome, mainly in chronic kidney disease, and peripheral neuropathy (slow acetylators, malnutrition); give pyridoxine and interrupt or reduce if neurotoxicity appears (SmPC 4.4). Pyrazinamide and ethambutol (separate products or 4-drug fixed-dose tablets) need thrice-weekly dosing at CrCl <30, so 4-drug fixed-dose tablets are unsuitable in CKD G4–G5 and on dialysis.
bands.short: No dose change; pyridoxine; neuro watch

hd.text: No dose change for either drug (ATS/CDC/IDSA 2016); give after hemodialysis on dialysis days. Add pyridoxine; watch for neuropathy and cerebellar signs (SmPC 4.4). Pyrazinamide and ethambutol (separate products or 4-drug fixed-dose tablets) need thrice-weekly dosing at CrCl <30, so 4-drug fixed-dose tablets are unsuitable in CKD G4–G5 and on dialysis.

pd.text: No dose change (CrCl <30 guidance; ATS/CDC/IDSA 2016, MSF); pyridoxine; watch for neuropathy and cerebellar signs.

dialyzable: Isoniazid: yes (hemodialysis advised for refractory overdose). Rifampicin: not stated (about 80% protein-bound) (SmPC 4.9, 5.2).
monitoring: Liver enzymes, bilirubin, creatinine, blood count and platelets at baseline; transaminases at least monthly if over 35 years, and every 2 to 4 weeks with liver disease or alcoholism. Neuropathy and cerebellar signs (especially CKD). Purpura or thrombocytopenia: stop rifampicin. Extensive enzyme-induction interactions (SmPC 4.4, 4.5).
